text:
jamie_support: FYI we have an urgent escalation from AcmeApp — their service started getting intermittent 401s from our API after their SSO key rotation last night. customer says it began ~2026-03-14T22:10Z. they see "invalid signature" and also some "token expired" spikes. any ideas? :rotating_light:
eli_security: Copy — can you paste a sample Authorization header + error logs (no PII)? quick theory: JWKS cache + key-rotation race or clock skew on customer's IdP causing exp/iat issues.
jamie_support: pasted the sanitized log snippet below from the customer (they redacted userids):
```
[2026-03-14T22:12:01Z] request_id=abc123 path=/v1/generate status=401 err="invalid signature" auth_kid=key_20260314 new_kid=key_20260315
[2026-03-14T22:12:05Z] request_id=abc124 path=/v1/embeddings status=401 err="token expired" iat=1700... exp=1700...
[2026-03-14T22:12:08Z] request_id=abc125 path=/v1/generate status=200
```
jamie_support: they say if they retry immediately sometimes it works, sometimes fails — very flaky.
devon_infra: sounds like two issues colliding: our JWKS cache still serving old key (so signature invalid) and the IdP rotated and issued tokens with slightly skewed clocks (so iat/exp borderline). we have a known JWKS cache TTL of 60s in the auth-client lib for hosted API. opsbot: incident-created for eng oncall (INC-2026-459).
els_security: can we reproduce quickly? jamie, can you ask AcmeApp for the `kid` they saw in the invalid signature logs and a sample token header (just the header, base64 part) and if they can curl our /.well-known/jwks.json when they see failures?
jamie_support: asked and they returned the token header and the kid: `key_20260315`. they also ran `curl -s https://api.redwood.ai/.well-known/jwks.json | jq .keys[].kid` and saw both `key_20260314` and `key_20260315` in the jwks response. they captured a failing request at 22:12:01 and when they immediately retried at 22:12:03 it passed.
devon_infra: interesting — that suggests our edge or an internal cache was still using the old jwks data for a micro-window. two possible caching locations: (1) local auth cache in the api-gateway pod (60s TTL), (2) CDN/proxy caching jwks response. check headers on jwks fetch (Cache-Control/ETag).
eli_security: also check client library behaviour: some JWT validation libs will try `kid` lookup first; if missing they fallback to trying all keys. if we only attempted to fetch by kid and fail, could lead to invalid signature until cache refresh. we should log if kid mismatch and fallback attempted.
jamie_support: they ran `curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/.well-known/jwks.json` and got: 
```
HTTP/2 200
cache-control: public, max-age=60
etag: "v20260314"
last-modified: Sun, 14 Mar 2026 21:55:00 GMT
```
jamie_support: so JWKS is updated (contains new key) but `etag` still `v20260314` which is confusing.
devon_infra: aha — that explains a race: origin updated keys but CDN returned stale cached copy for a short window; clients hitting the cache got old jwks json w/ old etag. when origin then updated ETag asynchronously it got inconsistent. need to check CDN invalidation rules and origin response.
els_security: proposed immediate mitigations: (a) add a server-side admin endpoint to force jwks refresh in api-gateway (for now we can restart gateway pods to flush local cache), (b) ask support to request customer to retry after 60s as temporary workaround, (c) increase allowed clock skew tolerance in validator to 120s for now to reduce exp/iat flakiness.
devon_infra: I can patch the admin endpoint `POST /admin/auth/jwks/refresh` in the gateway and add a metrics counter `auth.jwks_refresh_count` and `auth.jwks_cache_hits`. will do a quick canary deploy to staging.
eli_security: long-term fixes we should track in a ticket:
- serve JWKS with consistent ETag/Cache-Control and use `Cache-Control: no-cache` during rotations or push CDN purge.
- keep previous signing keys in signer service for a 24h overlap window so old tokens still validate (grace window), and similarly accept previous keys explicitly for N hours after rotation.
- add a small grace allowance for exp/iat check (configurable : default 60s -> 120s) and surface that in docs.
- augment validator to, upon kid lookup failure, attempt full-key search and log fallback.

sre_oncall: jamie, can you escalate to Customer Success to notify AcmeApp: 1) temporary retry guidance, 2) we're rolling gateway refresh now, 3) ETA for full fix. include them in the incident note.
jamie_support: done, CS notified and customer replies they can tolerate a short maintenance window. they asked for repro steps so they can test after our changes.
eli_security: repro steps for redwood eng to reproduce locally:
1. start a local jwks origin that serves keys A then atomically rotates to B.
2. set api-gateway jwks cache TTL to 60s and optionally put a caching proxy in front that honors Cache-Control.
3. issue tokens signed by B immediately after rotation; some gateway instances may still have A cached and see signature failures.

Sample commands:
```
# show jwks before/after
curl -s https://local-jwks.example/.well-known/jwks.json | jq .keys[].kid
# generate token using new key (B) header only:
echo '{"alg":"RS256","kid":"key-B"}' | base64 | tr -d '\n' ; echo '.'
# request to gateway with token
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" http://gateway.local/v1/generate
```

eli_security: also a quick check for signature error path — add an extra debug log when signature fails that includes `expected_kid`, `jwks_kids_seen`, and whether fallback search tried other keys (don't log token body).
devon_infra: rolling gateway patch to add admin refresh and extra logs now, will run canary in staging in ~15m and then prod if green. added also a temporary cron to purge CDN jwks cache on rotation.
opsbot: deployment started by devon_infra to staging (deploy-12345).
jamie_support: AcmeApp confirmed their retries are succeeding after we restarted one gateway instance. they will keep testing through the night. thanks all. :tada:
eli_security: follow-up action items summary (I'll open tickets):
- ENG-Auth-2026: add admin jwks refresh endpoint + metrics (devon)
- ENG-Auth-2026-2: CDN purge automation + rotation protocol (infra)
- ENG-Auth-2026-3: validator fallback logs + configurable clock skew (security)
- ENG-Auth-2026-4: signer keep-old-keys overlap policy + docs (product)

sre_oncall: marking incident IN-PROGRESS. will update SLA timeline.
jamie_support: closing loop with customer, they asked to be pinged when ENG-Auth-2026 is scheduled. I'll add them to the ticket watchers.
eli_security: thx everyone. we'll keep monitoring auth.jwks_mismatch_rate and auth.jwt_signature_errors. if numbers spike reopen incident.
opsbot: incident updated INC-2026-459 -> in_progress
